notes:
A phone or tablet can now take a project straight off the server. The sync settings list what the server already holds, and one tap downloads a project onto the device — no need to carry a file to it first.

Corylus now runs on Android phones and tablets and on iPhone and iPad. Projects live in the device's own Projects folder, a .cory file sent from another app opens straight in Corylus, and a compiled book goes out through the share sheet like any other file.

On a touch screen the binder reorders by dragging, a long press opens the menu that a right click opens on a computer, and the layout follows the width of the device, with its own focus mode for writing on a phone.

Phones and tablets keep a project in step over WebDAV, so what you wrote at the desk is already there when you open it on the phone. Pick your service from the list and Corylus fills in its address. pCloud and Nextcloud are the tested ones. The connection is marked beta while it is being used in the field.

The Story Bible's complete tag list can be opened, walked and closed from the keyboard, and its search field is readable in every theme. Before, on a dark theme the field was drawn white on white.

Story Bible tags can now be nested with a slash, such as faction/cerberos. The full tag list groups them, and choosing a group shows every entry with a tag inside it. While you filter, only the tags that still appear on matching entries are offered.

New: Manage tags, in the Story Bible's tag filter. Rename a tag in every entry at once, or rename it to an existing tag to merge the two. Corylus says how many entries will change and takes a snapshot of each one first.

Relationship maps draw their lines again on a computer that received the project by sync. Relationships are now read from the entries themselves, so they show up on every machine, including relationships that arrive while the project is open.

macOS: Corylus is not notarized yet, so Gatekeeper may say the app cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified. Right-click (or Control-click) Corylus.app, choose Open, then Open again. Only needed once per downloaded copy.
